relations.subject: Friedrich Max Müller
relations.evidence: He entered Leipzig University in 1841 to study philology, leaving behind his early interest in music and poetry. Müller received his Ph.D. degree in September 1843.

relations.subject: Friedrich Max Müller
relations.evidence: In 1844, Müller studied in Berlin with Friedrich Schelling. He began to translate the Upanishads for Schelling

relations.subject: Friedrich Max Müller
relations.evidence: and continued to research Sanskrit under Franz Bopp, the first systematic scholar of the Indo-European languages (IE).

relations.subject: Friedrich Max Müller
relations.evidence: In 1845, Müller moved to Paris to study Sanskrit under Eugène Burnouf.

relations.subject: Friedrich Max Müller
relations.role: deputy Taylorian professor of modern European languages
relations.evidence: In 1850 Müller was appointed deputy Taylorian professor of modern European languages at Oxford University.

relations.subject: Friedrich Max Müller
relations.role: Taylorian professor of modern European languages
relations.evidence: On succeeding to the full professorship in 1854, he received the full degree of M.A. by a decree of Convocation.

relations.subject: Friedrich Max Müller
relations.evidence: In 1858 he was elected to a life fellowship at All Souls' College.

relations.subject: Friedrich Max Müller
relations.evidence: Later in 1868, Müller became Oxford's first professor of comparative philology, a position founded on his behalf. He held this chair until his death, although he retired from its active duties in 1875.

relations.subject: Friedrich Max Müller
relations.evidence: In 1888, Müller was appointed Gifford Lecturer at the University of Glasgow. ... Over the next four years, Müller gave four series of lectures.
